$comment: IPC bindings with no production caller. Each entry needs a REASON,
because an entry without one is indistinguishable from a defect
somebody recorded instead of fixing. Ratchet: may shrink, never grow.
THIS FILE FAILS THE GUARD AS WRITTEN, deliberately: every entry
carries the placeholder and the guard rejects it by name. `--record`
gives you the LIST, never the licence. Replace each one with what
you found out, or the entry is not an exemption.

exempt.mobile/src/lib/attachments.ts:attachment: GENUINELY DEAD on this client. The §9.10 reconcile trio is registered in mobile/src-tauri/src/plugins/attachments/mod.rs and mirrored here, and no mobile screen reconciles a note's attachment references after an edit. The consequence is not cosmetic: without the apply, the catalog's per-note reference set drifts from the note body, which is what the GC floor reads. Pre-existing, exposed by blindness 3 above.

The read half of the trio. Answers which notes reference an attachment, which is what a delete confirmation needs in order to say what it is about to orphan. Mobile's AttachmentsSheet deletes without asking that question.

The other half of the trio above, and dead for the same reason: nothing on this client drops a deleted note's references. Same surface, same decision, recorded together so fixing one cannot silently leave the other.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/export.ts:vaultExportCanc: GENUINELY DEAD: mobile's export sheet offers no cancel affordance, so the app-managed ExportRuntime cancel flag has nothing to set it. The command and its ACL row exist; the button does not. Pre-existing, and adding the affordance is the export surface's call rather than this issue's.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/reminders.ts:createRawRem: Called by createReminderNotifier in the same file, which is itself dead: nothing outside mobile/src/lib/reminders.ts constructs a notifier at all. Recorded rather than deleted because it is the documented test seam (production must go through the wrapping factory, so the identifier crossing into Android SharedPreferences is opaque by construction), and because the surface above it is the known reminderPass gap rather than this line.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/reminders.ts:createRemind: GENUINELY DEAD, and the cost is stated in its own doc comment: on iOS an unauthorized add succeeds and then delivers nothing, so without this call the failure mode is a reminder that silently never fires. ReminderSettings.tsx imports only createExactAlarmApi. Same half-built surface as the entry above.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/snapshots.ts:snapshotPrun: GENUINELY DEAD on this client and recorded rather than deleted, because deleting it is the snapshots surface's call and not this issue's: mobile ships the snapshot list, preview and restore, and no pruning UI. The Rust command is registered, so the binding is the visible half of a surface that is half-built.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/transcribe.ts:readTranscr: GENUINELY DEAD: the §9.15 per-attachment extraction cache is written by the backend and read by nothing on this client, so an audio attachment's transcript is produced and never shown. Pre-existing.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-indices.ts:vaultInd: GENUINELY DEAD: mobile has no backlinks pane, so the folded-title-key candidate query has no consumer. The desktop twin drives its backlinks view from it. Part of the mobile graph/backlink parity gap rather than a defect this issue introduced.
GENUINELY DEAD, same surface as the entry above: degree-0 note ids feed a graph orphans filter mobile does not render.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-status.ts:probeVaul: GENUINELY DEAD, and the pair of entries is the point: this name is declared on BOTH clients and called on NEITHER, and each declaration was counting as the other's caller until the scan stopped treating a declaring file as a caller. Both clients route status through listVaults plus the runtime slot probe instead. Pre-existing, and deleting it is a two-client change outside this issue.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-unlock.ts:isVaultUn: GENUINELY DEAD: this client tracks the unlocked/locked state in its own store, seeded by the unlock call's own result and cleared by the lock choke point, so it never asks the backend. Exported to match the desktop twin's binding surface. Pre-existing.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-unlock.ts:reportUse: GENUINELY DEAD, and unlike the others this one is dead by DESIGN rather than by omission: mobile spawns no idle auto-lock loop (mobile/src-tauri/src/hooks.rs says so in effective_auto_lock_secs, and lib.rs spawns the sync loop and the poke supervisor and nothing else), because this client locks on backgrounding instead. Nothing reads the last_activity_millis atom here, so a heartbeat would feed a clock no one consults. The command stays registered because core/src/plugins/vault_unlock is shared.
exempt.src/lib/vault-status.ts:probeVaultStatus: The desktop half of the pair above. Same reason, same measurement: nothing outside its own file and its own doc comment names it.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setActiveWorkspa: Absent-on-mobile by design gap, not by decision: workspaces are a desktop bottom-bar surface and no mobile screen reads or writes the active workspace. Default only, and the binding stays so the twin prefs modules keep identical export names (myne-md/myne#486). Surfaced by the chokepoint widening (myne-md/myne#605).
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setBarItemsOrder: Same shape as setActiveWorkspace above: the bottom-bar reorder surface is desktop-only (resolveBarOrder/reorderByDrop have no mobile caller), so the order is default-only on this client. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setDailyDateForm: Consumed-but-unsettable, and that is a live defect rather than a gap: mobile/src/lib/daily.ts reads daily_date_format for the daily note's title and no mobile settings surface writes it (SettingsSheet carries no daily section), so a phone inherits whatever the desktop set and cannot change it. Recorded with the defect stated, not as approved absence.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setDailyFolder: Same defect as setDailyDateFormat above, same reader (mobile/src/lib/daily.ts), same missing writer: the daily note's folder is inherited and unchangeable on this client.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setDailyTemplate: Same defect as the two entries above: mobile/src/lib/daily.ts reads daily_template and nothing on this client writes it.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setEditorContent: Desktop editor-chrome pref with no mobile surface and no mobile reader outside the prefs default. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setEditorLayout: Desktop split-pane layout pref; the mobile editor has no panes and nothing reads this. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setHiddenBarItem: Desktop bottom-bar customization; no mobile bar to customize and no mobile reader. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setKeymapBinding: Nothing on this client reads or writes it — not even the prefs default object carries it. Mobile has no keymap surface at all. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setNewNoteLocati: Desktop new-note location pref; the mobile creation flow offers no location choice and nothing reads the default. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setRightPanelAct: Desktop right panel; no mobile equivalent and no mobile reader. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setRightPanelHid: Same surface as setRightPanelActiveTab above, same absence: no mobile reader, no mobile writer.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setRightPanelTab: Same surface as the two entries above: desktop-only panel order, default-only on this client.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/prefs.ts:setStartupOpen: Desktop startup behaviour; the mobile lifecycle (backgrounding, no cold-start note choice) has no such surface and nothing reads it. Twin-parity binding, surfaced by myne-md/myne#605.
exempt.src/lib/prefs.ts:setEditorSlashHidden: Pre-provisioned for a surface that does not exist: the slash-menu twin of toolbar-customize is an unbuilt follow-up (ToolbarCustomizeSettings.tsx header says so), so this setter has no caller and the pref has no reader. Recorded rather than deleted because the follow-up owns both halves.
exempt.src/lib/prefs.ts:setEditorSlashOrder: Same unbuilt follow-up as setEditorSlashHidden above: order pref with no ordering UI and no reader.
